basis: The definition locates the tumor in scrotal skin; vascular histology does not establish a separate cardiovascular organ lesion.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: this is a skin hemangioma; vascular histology alone does not add cardiovascular involvement.

basis: Serine synthesis disorder with brain malformations and ichthyosis; foot deformities 12/12 and toe syndactyly 7/12. Ablepharon 9/12 omitted at the four-organ cap.

decisions.ocular: none at cap: ablepharon affects 9/12, but universal limb malformations take the remaining slot.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: rocker-bottom feet in 12/12 and toe syndactyly in 7/12 establish common structural limb involvement.

basis: Vertebral closure defect with spinal cord injury. Common bladder/bowel denervation is separately diagnosed; direct urinary or intestinal damage in >=30% is not established.

decisions.renal: none: neurogenic bladder is a separate diagnosis secondary to spinal denervation; intrinsic urinary tract injury in >=30% is not established.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: neurogenic bowel is a separate diagnosis secondary to spinal denervation; common direct intestinal damage is not established.

basis: Oral clefts and renal agenesis each 2/3; choanal atresia 1/3 with reported lung hypoplasia. Ocular, adrenal and splenic anomalies at 1/3 omitted at cap; tiny series.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: choanal atresia in 1/3 meets the threshold; reported pulmonary hypoplasia supports prioritizing potentially lethal respiratory malformations.
decisions.ocular: none at cap: cataract and microphthalmia each occur in 1/3; renal, oral and respiratory malformations take priority.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none at cap: adrenal agenesis occurs in 1/3; renal, oral and respiratory malformations take priority.

basis: Intellectual disability and obstructive apnea define the syndrome. Visual dysfunction: astigmatism 2/2, amblyopia 1/1, nystagmus 3/3; skeletal damage prevalence remains uncertain.

decisions.ocular: involved: HPO documents visual impairment, including astigmatism 2/2 and amblyopia 1/1; these support the threshold, with limited denominators.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: skeletal malformations are reported in selected 1/1-2/2 samples; substantial skeletal impairment in >=30% of the syndrome is not established.

basis: Oxidative phosphorylation disorder; cerebral atrophy/regression, optic atrophy and hearing impairment each reported in 1/1. Aspiration does not establish intrinsic pulmonary disease.

decisions.neurologic: involved: cerebral atrophy, thalamic lesions and regression in 1/1 establish brain injury; the concept is defined by its metabolic defect.

basis: Periodontitis and characteristic pretibial plaques define this subtype; joint hypermobility 11/24 and scoliosis 9/27 support musculoskeletal involvement.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: characteristic pretibial plaques are a major diagnostic criterion (24/25); skin fragility affects 24/32.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: joint hypermobility 11/24 and scoliosis 9/27 meet the threshold; skeletal findings are secondary features of this periodontal subtype.

basis: Muscle degeneration, cataracts and conduction defects are defining features; intrinsic endocrine dysfunction, including insulin resistance and hypogonadism, affects >30%; four-organ cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: cardiac conduction defects are explicitly part of the disease definition.
decisions.ocular: primary: cataracts are explicitly part of the disease definition and common across the principal subtypes.

basis: Immune-mediated post-injury pericarditis; inflammatory pleuritis/pleural effusion occurs in roughly half and is a diagnostic feature of the post-cardiac-injury syndrome.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: immune-mediated pleural inflammation occurs in roughly 50% and contributes to syndrome criteria; pleura belongs to the pulmonary axis.

basis: BH4 recycling defect with usually benign hyperphenylalaninemia; developmental delay is 5-29%. Oculogyric crises at 30-79% do not alone establish lasting neurologic damage.

decisions.neurologic: none: oculogyric crises (30-79%) are episodic signs without established lasting impairment; developmental delay is only 5-29%.
